attribution.note: Marcus wrote this sentence in his own Substack post. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: 'That' refers back to human scientists still choosing the research goals. 'Not going to... next year' is a firm, unhedged forecast for 2026. The river-crossing clause is rhetoric, not a condition. The scope is faithful.

contract.note: Reading 'next year' as calendar 2026 and 'research goals' as substantive research direction is an ordinary, fair reading. The result depends on how strictly goal selection is distinguished from generating topics under a human brief, and the contract flags this correctly.

evidence.note: Nature, May 2026. Co-Scientist works from scientists' research objectives. This fits the forecast for one system, but it cannot establish the year-end position before the deadline.
Nature, March 2026. The AI Scientist generates ideas in an open-ended mode. The record does not show it repeatedly replacing human choices of substantive research direction.

arXiv, August 2026. Topics were generated by Gemini under a human-defined brief, and each run received the topic as a directive. This is AI topic generation inside a human programme, not clearly independent goal selection.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 31 December 2026, after the 28 October 2026 evaluation date. Under the contract, early resolution is possible only as contradicted, through a documented, repeated case of AI independently choosing substantive research goals. e2 and e3 show AI generating ideas and topics, but within human-set scaffolds or briefs, so they do not meet that bar. Continued human goal-setting cannot support the claim early, so the claim stays unresolved.
